children: Oil prices declined in Asia on Monday morning amid expectations that Russian diesel exports could help ease global fuel shortages.

President Trump said Friday his administration had reached an agreement for Russia to supply hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to supply over 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the U.S. and global markets, another 500,000 tons in November, and one million tons "immediately thereafter."

"This would mark a partial lifting of Russia's ban on diesel exports," Vivek Dhar, an analyst at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said in a report. "If these exports do eventuate, it will provide some relief to a market that is facing diesel shortages, but much will likely depend on Ukraine's ongoing attacks on Russian oil infrastructure," the analyst added.
Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures fell 1.5% to $90.49 a barrel, while front-month Brent crude oil futures declined 1.4% to $103.29 a barrel, according to ICE data.

However, the downward pressure on oil prices could be tempered by rising tensions in the Middle East. Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants conducted a missile attack on Saudi Arabia's international airport that killed at least 12 people and injured hundreds more on Saturday. The kingdom's military vowed a response, while President Trump told reporters that the U.S. could join Saudi strikes on the Houthis in light of the airport attack.

"From a sentiment perspective, developments in the Middle East and between Russia and Ukraine will be key drivers to start the week with two-sided risk on energy prices," said Skye Masters, head of Markets Research at National Australia Bank, in commentary.
Equity markets across Asia-Pacific were mixed. South Korea's Kospi fell 1.3%, and Australia's S&P/ASX 200 index was up 0.5%. Japan's financial markets were closed for a public holiday.
